title: Climate Risk in Plain Terms
summary: How climate change creates physical and transition risks for the firm, its clients and the wider financial system, and how firms identify, measure and manage them.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How climate change creates physical and transition risks for the firm, its clients and the wider financial system, and how firms identify, measure and manage them.
Learning Objectives: Distinguish physical and transition climate risks with examples
Explain how climate risk translates into credit, market, insurance and operational risk
Describe scenario analysis and climate targets in plain language
Syllabus: Physical risks: acute events and chronic change
Transition risks: policy, technology, market sentiment and litigation
How climate risk flows through to clients and the firm's balance sheet
Scenario analysis, financed emissions and transition plans explained
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including new joiners and colleagues who are new to sustainability topics
Client-facing, product, marketing, investment, operations and risk staff whose work touches ESG products or claims
Line managers who need their teams to discuss sustainability accurately with clients
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of sustainability or ESG is required. The programme is suitable for new joiners and as annual refresher training.
Core Reading: NGFS (2019), A Call for Action: Climate Change as a Source of Financial Risk
IOSCO (2023), Supervisory Practices to Address Greenwashing
